en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 4.6.
The Wholesome Triplet, Section on the Group of Defilements (Kilesagocchaka)

4.6.1. The Triplet of the Wholesome and the Dyad of the Defilements Dependent on an unwholesome state that is a defilement, an unwholesome state that is a defilement arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there is one; under object condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(Also in the section on co-nascence … and in the section on inquiry, it is one in all cases.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not associated with the defilements (*nokilesa*), a wholesome state that is not associated with the defilements arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not associated with the defilements, an unwholesome state that is not associated with the defilements arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a neutral, non-defiled state, a neutral, non-defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome, non-defiled state and a neutral, non-defiled state, a neutral, non-defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both an unwholesome, non-defiled state and a neutral, non-defiled state, a neutral, non-defiled state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause, nine; in the case of object, three; in the case of predominance, nine ... [and so on] ... in the case of result, one; in the case of non-disappearance, nine.
A wholesome state that is not associated with the taints is a condition, by way of root-cause condition, for a wholesome state that is not associated with the taints ... three.
An indeterminate state that is not associated with the taints is a condition, by way of root-cause condition, for an indeterminate state that is not associated with the taints. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-condition (hetu), there are four; in the case of object-condition (ārammaṇa), nine; in the case of predominance-condition (adhipati), ten ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance-condition (avigata), thirteen. 4.6.2.
The Faulty Triplet (Kusalattika) and the Corruptible Dyad (Saṅkilesikaduka):
The Tetrad of Conditions.
Dependent on a wholesome, defiled state, a wholesome, defiled state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on an unwholesome, defiled state, an unwholesome, defiled state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on an indeterminate, defiled state, an indeterminate, defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on wholesome and defiled states and indeterminate and defiled states, an indeterminate and defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on unwholesome and defiled states and indeterminate and defiled states, an indeterminate and defiled state arises by way of root condition.
[Under] root: nine; object: three ... pe ... fruition: one ... pe ... non-disappearance: nine. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on “Co-nascent” and “Associated” should also be expanded in detail.
A wholesome, defiled state is a condition for an unwholesome, defiled state by way of the root-condition … three.
An unwholesome, defiled state is a condition for an unwholesome, defiled state by way of the root-condition … three.
An indeterminate, defiled state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate, defiled state. (Abbreviated. [In the root-condition there are seven;
in the object-condition, nine; in the predominance-condition, nine ... pe ... in the non-disappearance-condition, thirteen.
Dependent on a wholesome, non-defiled state, a wholesome, non-defiled state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-defiled state, an indeterminate, non-defiled state arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Two for root; two for object … pe … one for repetition … pe … one for result … pe … two for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
(The section on co-nascence … and the section on association are also the same as the section on dependence.)
A wholesome, non-defiled state is a condition for a wholesome, non-defiled state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
A neutral, non-defiled state is a condition for a neutral, non-defiled state by way of the root-condition.
A neutral, non-defiled state is a condition for a neutral, non-defiled state by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
Condition. An indeterminate, non-defiled state is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*), for a wholesome, non-defiled state.

(Abbreviated. Under root-cause (*hetu*) there are two; under object, two; under predominance (*adhipati*), three; under proximity (*anantara*), two ... pe ... under decisive support (*upanissaya*), four ... pe ... under kamma, three; under result (*vipāka*), one ... pe ... under non-disappearance (*avigata*), two. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
4.6.3. *Kusalattika*, *Saṅkiliṭṭhaduka*:
Root and Object.
Dependent on an unwholesome, defiled state, an unwholesome, defiled state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under the root [condition] there is one; under the object [condition] there is one … pe … under the non-disappearance [condition] there is one. (Abbreviated.
(In the “Conascent” chapter … pe … and in the “Investigation” chapter, there is one in every instance.)
Dependent on a wholesome, non-defiled state, a wholesome, non-defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome, non-defiled state, an indeterminate, non-defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome, non-defiled state, both a wholesome, non-defiled state and an indeterminate, non-defiled state arise...
And states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-defiled state, an indeterminate, non-defiled state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome, non-defiled state and an indeterminate, non-defiled state, an indeterminate, non-defiled [state] arises...
A state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a wholesome, non-defiled state, a wholesome, non-defiled state arises by way of object-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-defiled state, an indeterminate, non-defiled state arises by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root-condition: five; object-condition: two; predominance-condition: five ... pe ... resultant-condition: one ... pe ...
non-disappearance-condition: five. (Abbreviated. (The section on co-nascence ... pe ... and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence.
A wholesome, undefiled state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome, undefiled state ... three.
An indeterminate, non-defiled state is a condition for an indeterminate, non-defiled state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
A wholesome, non-defiled state is a condition for a wholesome, non-defiled state by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—two [ways].
An indeterminate, non-defiled state is a condition for an indeterminate, non-defiled state by way of the object-condition—two [ways]. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu), there are four; in object condition (ārammaṇa), four; in predominance condition (adhipati), five; in proximity condition (anantara), four … pe … in conascence condition (sahajāta), five;

in mutuality condition (aññamañña), two; in dependence condition (nissaya), seven; in decisive support condition (upanissaya), four; in prenascence, postnascence, and repetition conditions (purejāta, pacchājāta, āsevana), two;

in kamma condition (kamma), four; in result condition (vipāka), one; in nutriment condition (āhāra) … pe … in path condition (magga), four; in association condition (sampayutta), two; in dissociation condition (vippayutta) … pe … [and so forth].
Three ... [and so on] ... seven in the case of non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
(As the section on questions in the *Kusala-ttika*, so it should be expanded.
4.6.4. *Kusala-ttika*, *Kilesa-sampayutta-duka* (The Triad of the Wholesome, the Dyad of the Associated with Defilements)
Root Condition:
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with defilements, an unwholesome state associated with defilements arises by way of root condition.
(This is similar to the Saṅkiliṭṭha-duka. 4.6.5. The Wholesome Triplet, the Defiled-Defilement Dyad.
Root Condition:
Dependent on a state that is both unwholesome and defiled, there arises a state that is both unwholesome and defiled by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root [condition], one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition], one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence, and likewise in the section on inquiry, it is the same in all cases.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, a wholesome state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement arises by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, an unwholesome state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement arises by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on a state that is indeterminate, subject to defilement, and not itself a defilement, there arises a state that is indeterminate, subject to defilement, and not itself a defilement, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, and an indeterminate state that is subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, there arises an indeterminate state that is subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, by way of root-condition.
[Likewise] dependent on an unwholesome state that is subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, and an indeterminate state that is subject to defilement and not itself a defilement...
Dependent on a neutral state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement, a neutral state that is subject to defilement and not itself a defilement arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are nine; under object [condition] three ... pe ... under resultant [condition] one ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition] nine.
(Abbreviated. (The "Conascent" chapter ... pe ... and the "Associated" chapter are the same as the "Dependent" chapter.)

A wholesome state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement. … three [answers].

An indeterminate state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state that is both subject to defilement and not itself a defilement. (Abbreviated. In the case of root-condition there are four;
in the case of object-condition, nine; in the case of predominance-condition, nine … pe … in the case of non-disappearance-condition, thirteen.

4.6.6. The Triplet of the Wholesome, the Dyad of Defiled by Defilements, and the Root Condition Dependent on a root unwholesome state that is both defiled by defilements and stained, there arises an unwholesome state that is both defiled by defilements and stained, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, one; in the case of object condition, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the section on co-nascence ... pe ... and in the entire section on inquiry, everywhere it is one.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome, defiled, and not itself a defilement, there arises a state that is unwholesome, defiled, and not itself a defilement, by way of root condition.
Under the root condition, one [answer] … pe … under the non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
(In the section on co-nascence as well … pe … in the section on inquiry as well, there is one in every instance. 4.6.7.
The Triplet on the Wholesome, the Couplets on Defilements and Association with Defilements.
Root Condition:

Dependent on a state that is both unwholesome and a defilement, as well as associated with defilements, there arises a state that is both unwholesome and a defilement, as well as associated with defilements, by way of root condition.
Under root [condition], one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition], one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence, ...pe... and in the section on inquiry, it is one in all instances.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is associated with defilements but is not itself a defilement, there arises an unwholesome state associated with defilements but not itself a defilement, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. One in the case of root; ...pe... one in the case of non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, it is always one.
4.6.8. The Triplet of the Wholesome, the Couple of the Defiled but Dissociated from the Defilements.
Root.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements but is subject to defilement, a wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements but is subject to defilement arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements but is subject to defilement, an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements but is subject to defilement arises by way of root condition. [Dependent on] a wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements...
Dependent on a defiled state, there arise wholesome states that are dissociated from the defilements, as well as both defiled and indeterminate states that are dissociated from the defilements,
by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements and is defiled, there arises an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements and is defiled, by way of the root condition.

Dependent on wholesome states that are dissociated from the defilements but are subject to defilement, and dependent on indeterminate states that are dissociated from the defilements but are subject to defilement, an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements but is subject to defilement arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. [In the root condition there are five;
in the object condition there are two ... pe ... in the resultant condition there is one ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition there are five. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on “Arising Together” and “Associated” are also similar to the section on “Dependent.

A wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements and is subject to defilement is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements and is subject to defilement. … three.

An indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements and is subject to defilement is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements and is subject to defilement. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are four; in the object condition, four; in the predominance condition, four … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, seven.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the defilements and not subject to defilement, a wholesome state arises that is dissociated from the defilements and not subject to defilement, by way of the root condition.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the defilements and not subject to defilement, an indeterminate state arises that is dissociated from the defilements and not subject to defilement, by way of the root condition.
In the case of root-cause, two; ... pe ... in the case of repetition, resultant, and non-disappearance, one; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, two.
(Abbreviated. (The section on co-nascence, ... pe ... and the section on association, are the same as the section on dependence.

A wholesome state dissociated from defilements and not subject to defilement is a condition, by way of root-cause condition, for a wholesome state dissociated from defilements and not subject to defilement.
An indeterminate state dissociated from defilement and non-proclivous is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state dissociated from defilement and non-proclivous.

(Abbreviated. Under root: two; under object: two; under predominance: three; under proximity: two … pe … under decisive support: four … pe … under kamma: three; under result: one … pe … under non-disappearance: two. (Abbreviated.
(The section on questions should be expanded in the same manner as the wholesome triad.)
The Section on the Fetters within the Wholesome Triplet is finished.
